description: i-Tree is a family of free tools that apply peer-reviewed USDA Forest Service science to estimate the benefits trees provide. It includes MyTree for quick assessment of individual trees, the flagship Eco tool, which imports tree inventories or field plot data to estimate structure and benefits such as air pollution removal, carbon storage, stormwater interception and energy effects, tree canopy assessment tools (Canopy, which samples points on aerial imagery, and Landscape, which combines US canopy and census data to prioritise planting and protection areas), and tools to plan planting, choose species by ecosystem service and forecast benefits. The tools are web-based or desktop and are offered free of charge with support. The site states that a change in USDA Forest Service policy has indefinitely halted traditional funding; a May 2026 update reports one-time funding from CAL FIRE and the Forest Service International Programs, while the lapse in funds for hosting and maintenance continues, so future availability is uncertain. Canopy and Landscape tools are limited to the continental United States, while Eco version 6 is adapted for Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, Mexico, Europe, Colombia, South Korea, Japan and New Zealand; results rely on regional coefficients. The tools are used to quantify urban green infrastructure, its contribution to heat mitigation, stormwater reduction and climate adaptation, and to build tree inventories for urban digital twins; related records are InVEST and the Copernicus Urban Atlas Street Tree Layer.
